submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole reads legal-instrument register (legalese), not the topic of law: it is strongly and steadily active across text written in the diction of binding legal documents - statutes, regulations, contracts, leases, terms, tax notices, software-licence disclaimers and court opinions - and near zero on ordinary prose, on journalism about the law, and on plain-English restatements of the same rules. Within such text it peaks on legal-procedural words and the function words embedded in that diction ('motion', 'appeal', 'affirm', 'ineffective', 'provisions', 'pursuant', 'liable'), and a legal-register word earlier in a sentence primes it for later tokens, so the same word ('moved', 'relied') is silent in plain prose.

DECISION AND ORDER

This proceeding arises from a complaint filed by the Commission alleging that the Respondent engaged in unfair or deceptive acts or practices in connection with the servicing of consumer accounts. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Respondent shall, within thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Order, provide a copy of this Order to each of its officers, managers, and employees having responsibility for the conduct described above, and shall obtain from each such person a signed statement acknowledging receipt.

The Respondent shall file a report in writing, under penalty of perjury, setting forth in reasonable detail the manner and form in which it has complied with this Order. The report shall be filed with the Commission within sixty (60) days after service of this Order. The Respondent may, within thirty (30) days of receipt of a request for additional information, move for an extension of time, provided that any such motion is accompanied by an affidavit showing good cause.

The provisions of this Order shall remain in effect for a period of twenty (20) years from the date of entry, and the Commission may, upon a showing of changed conditions, reopen the proceeding and modify or set aside any provision of this Order.
